turns.user: Tìm 3 tin AI mới nhất hôm nay và tóm tắt thành bullet có nguồn.
turns.assistant_text:
Here are the three latest news articles about AI today:

- **AI’s Economic Winners**  
  Source: [Council on Foreign Relations](https://www.cfr.org/articles/ais-economic-winners)  
  Summary: The article discusses how the development of AI is influencing the economic futures of different countries and their geoeconomic abilities, which will help define the global balance of power. It emphasizes the importance of digital infrastructure and the debate on whether AI will augment or replace workers.

- **An AI Data Center is Being Built on My Grandma's Garden**  
  Source: [National Catholic Reporter](https://www.ncronline.org/opinion/guest-voices/ai-data-center-being-built-my-grandmas-garden)  
  Summary: This piece reflects on the impact of AI on human dignity and the environment, highlighting concerns about the energy and water requirements of AI systems. The author shares personal feelings about the transformation of farmland into a data center, raising questions about sustainability and the physical impact of AI infrastructure.

- **The AI Future Is for Everyone**  
  Source: [The Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/opinion/the-ai-future-is-for-everyone-a0c24e20)  
  Summary: Mark Zuckerberg discusses the potential of AI to enhance human capabilities and improve various aspects of life, including health and relationships. The article argues against centralized power, suggesting that it stifles human potential and innovation.

Feel free to ask if you need more information!

items.title: AI’s Economic Winners | Council on Foreign Relations
items.summary: That trend has now collided with a separate structural change that is advancing at an incredible pace: the development of artificial intelligence (AI). The influence that AI has on different countries’ economic futures and resulting geoeconomic abilities will help define the global balance of power. [...] AI development also requires sufficient digital infrastructure, including data and computing systems. Further, it needs computer hardware that goes well beyond chips and land for data centers to store and process data, which in turn requires sufficient water to cool systems and energy to run systems. [...] While the widespread use of AI in a country is a critical step to seeing economic benefits, it also matters how the technology is used. To what degree does AI augment workers (that is, increase their productivity) versus replace workers and increase corporate efficiency? There is also a related debate around how quickly AI-fueled innovation can create new opportunities for labor, thus mitigating AI-related job displacement.

items.title: An AI data center is being built on my grandma's garden
items.summary: In his recent encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, Pope Leo lifts up the concern of human dignity in light of increasing technological advances. He states that we are facing a decision; either to create a world where "the dignity of every person is safeguarded [and] justice is promoted" or to create an "inhumane and more unjust world." He goes on to directly confront AI and caution us to realize that "technological innovations, including artificial intelligence, are not neutral, for they can either [...] He also reminds us to think of the physical impact of utilizing AI while reminding us that data centers are not neutral. He states: "Current AI systems require enormous amounts of energy and water … which requires an extensive network of machines, cables, data centers and energy-intensive infrastructure … It is essential to develop more sustainable technological solutions." [...] It’s hard to describe the feeling I have, deep in my gut, when I think about what is happening to the land. Concrete is being poured over what was once farmland. Land once traveled by bicyclists and monarch butterflies alike is becoming a place to store data and help train AI. The noise and light pollution is disrupting residents, and animals are being forced to find new places to traverse.

We are fortunate to live at an incredible moment in history. In the next few years, people will be able to use superintelligence beyond human capacity to create and discover extraordinary new things, build new businesses, express our ideas, learn new concepts, and improve our lives, health, relationships and careers.
